Question: terraform init -migrate-state (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Re-initializes after a backend change and copies the existing state into the new backend.

Question: terraform init -reconfigure (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Uses the new backend configuration and ignores the saved one without copying any state across.

Question: terraform init -upgrade (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Ignores the versions recorded in the lock file and selects the newest providers and modules that match the constraints.

Question: Partial backend configuration (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Leaving backend settings out of the backend block and supplying them at init with -backend-config, because backend blocks cannot use variables.

Question: terraform plan -out (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Saves the proposed actions to a plan file that terraform apply can later execute exactly, without prompting.

Question: Refresh-only mode (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Plan or apply with -refresh-only, which updates state to match real infrastructure without proposing any infrastructure changes.

Question: replace (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Plan or apply option that forces replacement of one resource instance; the reviewable successor to terraform taint.

Question: target (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Option that limits planning to one resource or module and its dependencies; intended only for exceptional recovery situations.

Question: terraform destroy (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Shortcut for terraform apply -destroy, which plans and executes removal of every resource the configuration manages.

Question: terraform state rm (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Removes an address from state so Terraform stops managing the object, without destroying the real resource.

Question: import block (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Declarative import (Terraform 1.5 and later) that brings an existing object into state as part of plan and apply.

Question: generate-config-out (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Plan option that writes HCL for import blocks whose target has no resource block yet; experimental in 1.5 and 1.6.

Question: moved block (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Declarative record that a resource or module changed address, so Terraform updates state instead of destroying and recreating.

Question: terraform force-unlock (manage resource lifecycle)
Answer: Removes a stale state lock by ID; it does not stop a running operation, so confirm the lock holder is dead first.

Question: validation block (dynamic configuration)
Answer: Rule inside a variable block that rejects bad input before planning; in Terraform 1.6 it may reference only its own variable.

Question: precondition (dynamic configuration)
Answer: Custom condition in a lifecycle block or output that must hold before the object is planned, failing the run if false.

Question: postcondition (dynamic configuration)
Answer: Custom condition in a resource or data source lifecycle block that checks the result, using self, and fails the run if false.

Question: check block (dynamic configuration)
Answer: Top-level assertion (Terraform 1.5 and later) evaluated after plan and apply that reports failures as warnings only.

Question: terraform test (dynamic configuration)
Answer: Command, generally available in Terraform 1.6, that runs .tftest.hcl files with run blocks, assertions and expect_failures.

Question: expect_failures (dynamic configuration)
Answer: List in a terraform test run block naming checkable objects whose validation is expected to fail, used to test validation rules.

Question: Data source (dynamic configuration)
Answer: Read-only lookup of existing information from a provider, referenced as data.TYPE.NAME and read at plan time when possible.

Question: for_each (dynamic configuration)
Answer: Meta-argument that creates one instance per key of a map or set of strings, addressed by key; keys must be known at plan time.

Question: count (dynamic configuration)
Answer: Meta-argument that creates a numbered set of instances addressed by index; best for zero-or-one and truly identical copies.

Question: dynamic block (dynamic configuration)
Answer: Construct that generates repeated nested blocks inside a resource from a collection, using a content block and an iterator.

Question: replace_triggered_by (dynamic configuration)
Answer: Lifecycle argument (Terraform 1.2 and later) that replaces a resource when a referenced resource or attribute changes.

Question: optional() (dynamic configuration)
Answer: Object type modifier (Terraform 1.3 and later) that lets callers omit an attribute, optionally supplying a default value.

Question: sensitive (dynamic configuration)
Answer: Flag on variables and outputs that redacts values from CLI output; the values are still stored in plain text in state.

Question: Dynamic secrets (dynamic configuration)
Answer: Short-lived credentials generated on demand, for example by Vault, so any copy written to Terraform state soon expires.

Question: Locking is native (collaborative workflows)
Answer: the backend takes a lease on the state blob. There is no extra table to create.

Question: required_version (collaborative workflows)
Answer: Setting in the terraform block that constrains which Terraform CLI versions may run the configuration.

Question: Pessimistic constraint (~>) (collaborative workflows)
Answer: Version operator that lets only the rightmost given part increase, so ~> 5.30 means at least 5.30 and below 6.0.

Question: .terraform.lock.hcl (collaborative workflows)
Answer: Dependency lock file recording the exact provider versions and checksums chosen by init; it does not record module versions.

Question: terraform providers lock (collaborative workflows)
Answer: Command that adds provider checksums for listed platforms to the lock file so every OS and architecture can verify packages.

Question: S3 backend locking (collaborative workflows)
Answer: In Terraform 1.6 the S3 backend locks state with a DynamoDB table whose partition key is LockID, set via dynamodb_table.

Question: azurerm backend locking (collaborative workflows)
Answer: The azurerm backend locks state natively by taking a lease on the state blob, so no extra lock resource is needed.

Question: cloud block (collaborative workflows)
Answer: Terraform block (1.1 and later) that connects a configuration to HCP Terraform for state and runs, replacing backend remote.

Question: TF_IN_AUTOMATION (collaborative workflows)
Answer: Environment variable that, when set to any non-empty value, adjusts output so it does not suggest commands a pipeline cannot run.

Question: input=false (collaborative workflows)
Answer: Option that makes Terraform fail instead of prompting for missing values, essential for unattended pipelines; TF_INPUT=0 is equivalent.

Question: detailed-exitcode (collaborative workflows)
Answer: Plan option returning exit code 0 for no changes, 1 for an error and 2 when changes are present.

Question: terraform_remote_state (collaborative workflows)
Answer: Data source that reads another configuration's root outputs but requires read access to that entire state snapshot.

Question: tfe_outputs (collaborative workflows)
Answer: tfe provider data source that reads HCP Terraform workspace outputs without full state access; HashiCorp recommends it over remote state.

Question: CLI workspaces (collaborative workflows)
Answer: Named states for one configuration in one backend, selected with terraform workspace; distinct from HCP Terraform workspaces.

Question: Root module (modules)
Answer: The configuration in the working directory where Terraform runs; it calls child modules and owns provider configuration.

Question: Child module (modules)
Answer: A module called from another module with a module block, whose outputs are the only values the caller can read.

Question: Standard module structure (modules)
Answer: HashiCorp's recommended layout with main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, a README, examples and nested modules directories.

Question: Module source (modules)
Answer: The source argument of a module block: a local path, registry address, private registry address, Git URL or archive URL.

Question: Module version argument (modules)
Answer: Version constraint on a module block that works only for registry sources; Git sources pin with ?ref= instead.

Question: configuration_aliases (modules)
Answer: required_providers setting in a module that declares which aliased provider configurations the caller must pass in.

Question: Semantic versioning (modules)
Answer: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH scheme where a major bump signals a breaking change, minor a compatible feature and patch a fix.

Question: Registry module naming (modules)
Answer: Repositories published to the Terraform registry are named terraform-PROVIDER-NAME and use semver tags for versions.

Question: moved block in a module (modules)
Answer: A moved block placed inside a shared module so every consumer's state is updated automatically when they upgrade.

Question: Refactor into a module (modules)
Answer: Move resources into a module and add moved blocks from old root addresses to module addresses so plan shows no replacements.

Question: Double slash in a source (modules)
Answer: The // in a module source selects a subdirectory inside a Git repository or archive, for example repo.git//modules/vpc.

Question: Terraform Core (providers)
Answer: The terraform binary that reads configuration, builds the graph, manages state and drives providers, without knowing any cloud API.

Question: Provider plugin (providers)
Answer: Separate executable that Core runs as a child process and calls over gRPC to validate, plan and apply resources for one API.

Question: Provider source address (providers)
Answer: Global provider identifier in the form hostname/namespace/type, where the hostname defaults to registry.terraform.io.

Question: required_providers (providers)
Answer: terraform block setting that maps local provider names to source addresses and version constraints.

Question: Provider alias (providers)
Answer: Additional named configuration of a provider, selected with provider = NAME.ALIAS on resources, data sources and modules.

Question: providers map (providers)
Answer: Module block argument that passes specific provider configurations, including aliases, from the caller to a child module.

Question: Registry tiers (providers)
Answer: Terraform Registry labels for providers: official (HashiCorp-owned), partner (partner-owned, reviewed) and community.

Question: Provider mirror (providers)
Answer: Local filesystem or network copy of provider packages, configured in the CLI config file for restricted networks.

Question: terraform state replace-provider (providers)
Answer: Command that reassigns resources in state from one provider source address to another, for example after a namespace move.

Question: TF_LOG (providers)
Answer: Environment variable enabling logs at TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR or JSON; TF_LOG_PATH writes them to a file.

Question: TF_LOG_PROVIDER (providers)
Answer: Environment variable that enables logging for provider plugins only, at the same levels as TF_LOG.

Question: TF_LOG_CORE (providers)
Answer: Environment variable that enables logging for Terraform Core only, at the same levels as TF_LOG.

Question: HCP Terraform workspace (hcp terraform)
Answer: Unit holding one configuration with its state, variables, runs, settings and team access in HCP Terraform.

Question: Speculative plan (hcp terraform)
Answer: Plan-only run, for example on a pull request, that cannot be applied and does not lock the workspace.

Question: Run task (hcp terraform)
Answer: External service called at the pre-plan, post-plan, pre-apply or post-apply stage, with advisory or mandatory enforcement.

Question: Run trigger (hcp terraform)
Answer: Workspace link that queues a run in a workspace after a named source workspace applies successfully.

Question: Execution mode (hcp terraform)
Answer: Workspace setting choosing where runs execute: remote on HCP Terraform, local on your machine, or on self-hosted agents.

Question: Variable set (hcp terraform)
Answer: Reusable group of variables applied globally, to projects or to workspaces; priority sets override all other values.

Question: Project roles (hcp terraform)
Answer: Fixed project permission sets in HCP Terraform: Read, Write, Maintain and Admin, plus Custom.

Question: Workspace roles (hcp terraform)
Answer: Fixed workspace permission sets in HCP Terraform: Read, Plan, Write and Admin, plus Custom.

Question: Dynamic provider credentials (hcp terraform)
Answer: Per-run OIDC tokens from HCP Terraform exchanged for short-lived cloud credentials, removing stored static keys.

Question: TFC_AWS_PROVIDER_AUTH (hcp terraform)
Answer: Workspace environment variable that, set to true with TFC_AWS_RUN_ROLE_ARN, enables dynamic credentials for AWS.

Question: Policy set (hcp terraform)
Answer: Group of Sentinel or OPA policies applied globally, to projects or to workspaces, evaluated on every run in scope.

Question: Soft-mandatory (hcp terraform)
Answer: Sentinel enforcement level where a failed policy stops the run but a user with Manage policy overrides can override it.

Question: Hard-mandatory (hcp terraform)
Answer: Sentinel enforcement level where a failed policy stops the run and, by default, cannot be overridden.

Question: Health assessments (hcp terraform)
Answer: Scheduled drift detection and continuous validation of check blocks that report problems without remediating them.
